answer_text:
The post – mortem findings:
Of strangulation by a rope:
1- General signs of mechanical anoxia:
• Dark violet or blue hypostasis.

• Proptosis of eyeballs.

• Viscera and brain are congested.
• Sub pericardial and meningeal petichial hemorrhages.
• Blood is dark and fluid.

• The rope may be found tied on the neck.
• There I constriction (ligature) mark on the neck, which is at a low level and transverse, and shows the pattern of rope with abrasions.
• Contusions and lacerations in the neck.
• The hyoid bone is broken inwards.

3- Signs of rape:
• General resistance signs may not be present, as young girls cannot resist as older females. There may be nail abrasions on the mouth or medial aspect of thighs and on the vulva.
• The hymen is torn, & tears reach the vaginal wall, with clotted blood and hyperemia.

A 23 years old male hit a 40 years old man by a stick on his head. Some hair was found on the stick. The victim was transmitted to the hospital in a drowsy state. X-ray head revealed a linear (fissure) fracture and extradural hemorrhage. Few hours later full signs and symptoms of compression were noted.
a. Verify the age of both the victim and assailant by doing an X-ray (one site for each age).
b. What caused this extradural hemorrhage?
c. What is the clinical picture of cerebral compression?
d. Discuss the medicolegal importance of examination of hair present on the stick?
answer_text:
a. a) Age 23 years old male is identified by: union of epiphysis of the sternal end of clavicle with its shaft by doing an x-ray to the chest (clavicle).
b) Age 40 years old man by: chest x-ray to see union of xiphoid process with body of sternum.
b. Extradural hemorrhage: was caused by trauma by the stick to the parieto temporal area and tear or rupture to one of middle meningeal artery branches as a result of transaction by the fissure fracture leading to gradual collection of hematoma.
c. Clinical picture of cerebral compression:
If the patient is conscious and the compression is gradual he complains of:
1) Drowsiness, blurring of vision and severe occipital headache.
Effortless central vomiting, stupor then coma takes place.
2) Rigidity of the back of the neck due to stretch of the basal meninges.
I. Irritation Phase:
3) Blood pressure rises until it may reach a very high level stimulation of VMC.
4) Pulse is slow due to stimulation of vagal center and full due to stimulation of vasomotor center.
5) Face is congested.
6) Respiration is deep and slow at 1st due to irritation of respiratory center.
7) Fever due to derangement of heat regulating center.
8) Pupils are unequal. Miosis starts at the side of compression due to irritation of occulomotor center. When compression is reflected to the opposite side -> constriction in the opposite side.
9) Twitches and convulsions start in the opposite side of compression (contralateral side of the lesion) due to irritation neurosis of pyramidal tract.
10) Conjugate deviation of both eyes to the side of compression.
11) CSF is under pressure.
NB. 3(8) and (9) are called lateralizing signs of compression and are diagnostic of the side of compression.
II. Paralytic Stage:
1) Face is cyanosed.
2) Hypotension due to paralysis of VMC.
3) Pulse is rapid and weak.
4) Respiration becomes stertorous due to movement of flaccid soft palate and falling back of the tongue. Cheyne Stokes respiration and asphyxial death due to medullary herniation may occur.
5) Pupils on the same side become dilated followed by miosis of the other side and then dilatation due to paralysis. Terminally both pupils are dilated and fixed before death.
6) Paralysis on the contralateral side starts which is at first flaccid. Later on, true spastic hemiplegia with exaggerated reflexes.

a. That the hair present is human

Causes and medicolegal importance of persistent vegetative state. (6 Marks)
answer_text: The term "persistent vegetative state" was introduced to describe the condition of patients with severe brain damage in whom coma has progressed to a state of "wakefulness without awareness." In persistent vegetative state the individual loses the higher cerebral powers of the brain, but the functions of the brainstem, such as respiration (breathing) and circulation, remain relatively intact. The distinguishing feature of the persistent vegetative state is an irregular but cyclic state of circadian sleep and wake cycles, unaccompanied by any detectable expression of self-awareness. Furthermore, they can grind their teeth, swallow, smile, shed tears, grunt, moan, or scream without any reason. Their heads and eyes can follow a moving object or move towards a loud sound. These conditions may follow hypoxic encephalopathy, massive cerebral infarcts, head trauma or prolonged severe hypoglycemia. The medical care team should concentrate on preventing infections and maintaining the patient's physical state as much as possible. Such maintenance includes preventing pneumonia and bed sores and providing balanced nutrition. Medicolegal Importance: Withholding or withdrawing life-sustaining treatment, and cessation of life-support measures is considered by many as a form of passive euthanasia. The term "passive euthanasia" can be defined as the intentional ending of one's life by a medical omission when death is not imminent.

The dangers of criminal abortion are:
